boards.title: Your First Weekend at University of North Florida, Shared as Cards
boards.description: A low-pressure, under-21-safe first-weekend route through documented UNF services, gathering spots, arts spaces, recreation, and campus nature.

cards.title: Start at the Student Union
cards.subtitle: Friday afternoon · Building 58
cards.notes: Use the first-floor services and floor maps to orient yourself, then pick one nearby destination before heading deeper into campus.
cards.short_summary: A practical first landmark with food, services, meeting rooms, and student-facing offices.
cards.evidence_claim: UNF’s Student Union map lists the John A. Delaney Student Union as Building 58 and identifies services across its east and west wings.
cards.source_title: John A. Delaney Student Union Maps
cards.access_notes: Consult the current Student Union map for room locations and access.

cards.title: Find a way to get involved
cards.subtitle: Friday afternoon · Student Union East, first floor
cards.notes: Stop by the Osprey Involvement Center to identify registered organizations or campus activities that fit your interests.
cards.short_summary: A named Student Union destination for connecting with campus involvement.
cards.evidence_claim: UNF’s Student Union map lists the SG Osprey Involvement Center on the east wing’s first level.
cards.source_title: John A. Delaney Student Union Maps
cards.access_notes: Located in the Student Union; check current office availability before visiting.

cards.title: Take a food-court break
cards.subtitle: Friday evening · Student Union West, Suite 1600
cards.notes: Choose a meal or snack from the documented food-court vendors, then use the pause to map tomorrow’s campus stops.
cards.short_summary: A central on-campus dining stop with several named vendors in one location.
cards.evidence_claim: UNF lists Panda Express, Einstein Bros Bagels, Halal Shack, and Qdoba in the Student Union’s food court at Building 58W, Suite 1600.
cards.access_notes: Food purchases may be required; vendor offerings and operating times can change.

cards.title: Settle in at the Boathouse
cards.subtitle: Friday evening · Student Union West, Suite 2600
cards.notes: Use the renovated second-floor restaurant as a recognizable meetup point and confirm current service before planning a meal there.
cards.short_summary: A named Student Union restaurant with updated seating and space to plug in devices.
cards.evidence_claim: UNF identifies The Boathouse in Building 58W, Suite 2600; its newsroom describes its second-floor Student Union location and renovated seating.
cards.access_notes: Restaurant service and purchases apply; confirm current availability with the venue.

cards.title: Make the library your Saturday anchor
cards.subtitle: Saturday morning · Building 12
cards.notes: Walk through Carpenter Library, save its contact information, and check the current options for research help, spaces, or lending.
cards.short_summary: UNF’s main library and a reliable campus landmark for academic support.
cards.evidence_claim: UNF identifies Thomas G. Carpenter Library as Building 12 and states that the library offers iPad checkout for students.
cards.access_notes: Student borrowing and spaces may have eligibility or availability requirements.

cards.entity_name: Cynthia and Walter R. Graham, Jr., M.D. Student Art Gallery
cards.title: Look through the student art gallery
cards.subtitle: Saturday late morning · Carpenter Library, second floor
cards.notes: Add a short gallery stop while you are in the library and look for work from UNF’s student art community.
cards.short_summary: A dedicated student gallery space inside the library.
cards.evidence_claim: UNF states that the Graham Student Art Gallery is on the second floor of the UNF Library and was created through a library-art department collaboration.
cards.access_notes: Check current gallery access and exhibitions before making a special trip.

cards.title: See what is on view at Lufrano
cards.subtitle: Saturday afternoon · Student Union East, Suite 2401
cards.notes: Visit the second-floor gallery for a focused art stop, and use the posted exhibition information to guide your viewing.
cards.short_summary: A Student Union gallery presenting visual art connected to cultural experiences and perspectives.
cards.evidence_claim: UNF says the Lufrano Intercultural Gallery is in Student Union Building 58E, Suite 2401, and is dedicated to visual art reflecting varied cultural experiences.
cards.access_notes: UNF lists gallery hours as Monday–Thursday, 10 a.m.–4 p.m.; verify before visiting.

cards.title: Check out RecWell’s main facility
cards.subtitle: Saturday afternoon · Building 61
cards.notes: Tour the Student Wellness Complex and review current recreation options so you know where to return for a future workout or class.
cards.short_summary: UNF RecWell’s named wellness facility with group-fitness space.
cards.evidence_claim: UNF’s Recreation and Wellness page identifies the Student Wellness Complex as Building 61 and lists group fitness studios on its first floor.
cards.access_notes: Facility access and programs may require current student eligibility; review RecWell’s current hours.

cards.title: Locate the Competition Pool
cards.subtitle: Saturday afternoon · Building 25
cards.notes: Find the pool complex now, then check the live schedule before returning for swimming or another aquatics program.
cards.short_summary: A named RecWell aquatics facility with an Olympic-size swimming pool.
cards.evidence_claim: UNF identifies the Competition Pool Complex as Building 25 and lists an Olympic Size Swimming Pool and locker rooms.
cards.access_notes: Pool access and hours are subject to current RecWell operations; check before visiting.

cards.title: End with a garden walk
cards.subtitle: Sunday daytime · UNF Botanical Garden
cards.notes: Take a daylight walk through the Bamboo Garden and use the interpretive setting as a calm close to your first campus weekend.
cards.short_summary: A named campus garden centered on clumping bamboo species.
cards.evidence_claim: UNF’s Botanical Garden visitor guide lists the Bamboo Garden and describes it as a place to encounter clumping bamboo through texture, shape, and sound.
cards.access_notes: Visit during daylight and follow current campus and garden guidance.
